domain.basis: Full-report domain review in inference economics, caching, retries and serving capacity, independently performed by /root/independent_domain_b. Read every line of the current report and its current instructions; task and effective requirements match those already read. Prior TE-U2 reading was reused only after confirming the full report contains that exact current unit, and the entire assembled text was still read. (1) Cost boundaries are coherent: DeepSeek-V3 original Table 1 supports 2.788M H800 hours and $5.576M at an assumed $2/hour, with prior research/ablations excluded; Meta's original card supplies H100 hours and license/architecture without a dollar-cost claim; the Cottier original methods distinguish rental, depreciated hardware/energy and wider development. The investment-allocation formula and four scenarios are dimensionally correct and expressly hypothetical. (2) Serving discussion retains prefill/decode, KV, batching, quantization, MoE and reliability distinctions. DistServe's original §6.1 and runtime limitations support OPT/FP16, 32 A100-80GB GPUs, Poisson arrivals and unimplemented fault tolerance; the manuscript does not transfer that experiment's speedup into a current frontier-model unit cost. (3) Original historical launch material and cutoff pricing support the selected tariffs, dates, currency and tier distinctions. Checked GPT-6.1 Sol's official >272K whole-request price boundary; OpenAI write categories/lifetime upgrades are not double-counted or confused with guaranteed physical reuse. Claude/Gemini/DeepSeek cache and tool contracts remain distinct. Local tokenizer code and existing exact-string results support the table without treating six strings as language-wide or billed endpoint evidence. (4) Reconfirmed the complete support, document and agent passages against the earlier independently read code, outputs and original tariff/terms: bounded conditional retries, unresolved-task numerator costs, acceptance denominators, paid compaction/fallback, cache writes/reads and human repair are explicit. The 4x-output sensitivity remains correctly restricted to fixed input/cache/path/quality assumptions, so no unsupported retained-history inference returns in the synthesis. (5) Independently checked the Azure original Retail Prices JSON against the cited official hardware table: $13.96/hour is the whole Linux non-Spot/non-Low-Priority East US node, and two 94GB H100 NVL GPUs, 80 vCPUs, 640 GiB RAM and temporary storage are accurately distinguished. Reviewed the concurrency preprint's original co-tenant setup, output-only cost denominator and Figure 5 input-billing claim: the report correctly rejects the numerical crossover as procurement evidence while retaining the utilization mechanism. The manuscript's separate 10-rps capacity and quality figures are conspicuously assumptions; $13,490.80/month, 26.28M request capacity, 3.764M Sonnet crossover, infeasible 75.283M Haiku crossover, quality-adjusted 4.235M and two-node 6.608M crossovers agree with the code and preserved outputs. The formula F*q_A/(a*q_L) has the right acceptance denominators, and standby versus active-active capacity is distinguished. (6) NVIDIA original results and Microsoft official earnings/metric pages support the company/Cloud figures. These are not used to invent a model margin. Contribution arithmetic, the application support-cost example, value-chain roles and distinctions among cash savings, released labor capacity, willingness to pay and revenue remain conditional and economically meaningful. (7) Procurement recommendations follow those boundaries: no measured open-model/API quality parity, guaranteed latency, confidential discount or realized productivity gain is invented. No required domain correction found in this complete version. No author calculation, tokenizer execution or model experiment was rerun; this is content-domain assessment, not audit/final acceptance.
